name: n4_station_health
description: Station health in one call, each section answered on its own: system (the SystemService slots by their station names: CPU usage in percent, memory as the station reports it plus memory_used_percent, version, host, time), points (total, ok, null_only, not_ok_count, a count per status flag in by_flag and the not-ok ones in not_ok, up to max_not_ok; ok is no flag, null_only is the flag null alone, a point with no value and not a fault, and not ok is any other flag, so ok + null_only + not_ok_count = total; proxy is the points whose proxy extension is not control:NullProxyExt, the ones a licence counts), networks and devices (the same, plus disabled and each not-ok entry's name, type and enabled), totals (the n4_inventory totals of the same rows, with rows_truncated when a query feeding them was cut), capacity (resources: the Global Capacity table of the spy metrics page, per resource used and limit, unlimited true where the station shows no limit, and live; recount: its recount times) and elapsed_ms. Two counts sit side by side in a resource: used is the licence's own tally, the number to quote against limit for licensing, and it only grows until a capacity recount or a station restart; live is what the station really holds now (networks, devices and proxy points of the whole station; null for a resource this tool does not count or when base is a subtree). may_be_inflated is true, with an inflation_note, when a used is above its live or the recount has never run. A section that fails is {error} and the others still answer. capacity is null with a capacity_note when the spy metrics page is unreachable or holds no Global Capacity table: never a guessed count. capacity_truncated is true, and capacity_note says so, when the page was cut before it was read whole, so resources may be missing; rows of the table that do not match its header are counted in capacity_note. In a section, truncated means not_ok was cut at max_not_ok (not_ok_count is whole) and rows_truncated means the query hit max_rows, so the counts are lower bounds. A status the station did not answer counts under the flag unknown and as not ok, never as ok. license is the licence manager page (spy sysManagers/licenseManager) in short: licenses (name, expires, valid, with state when not valid, and days_left counted from the station's own date, the day of system.systemTime; null for never, for an expiry that is not a date or when that date is unknown; up to 100, licenses_count when more), nearest_expiry (the earliest dated expiry among licences, certificates and features, with same_date: how many share it), expired (what is already past; null when the station date is unknown) and a warning when the nearest expiry is 60 days away or fewer, or past, when a licence is not reported valid, or when an expiry could not be read as a date; note says what the reading could not do; {error} when the page was not read, saying which case it is (no permission, no such page, not HTML, not a licence page), never an empty licence. n4_license_info has the whole of it.

base.description: Subtree ORD of the point, network and device counts, default station:|slot:/

max_not_ok.description: Cap of the not-ok entries listed per section

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds
